findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC2 (abstain / no content vote) with AC3+design ('replaces the stale -1'): state ONE recorded-block shape (vote-less-defer OR coverage-gap -1) and define exactly what the recovery loop keys on and what it replaces.
evidence: AC2: 'the review-bot casts no LLM-Review content vote (abstains)'
AC3 / design: 'same-patchset re-vote that cleanly REPLACES the stale -1'

Incumbent code already models BOTH shapes distinctly: RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS defer VOTE-LESS for reconciler re-drive, escalating to a fail-closed -1 only on retry exhaustion (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:66-74); recheck-review eligibility keys on a coverage-gap -1 vs a real 'finding' -1 (src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py:232-245,307-331)
findings.finding: The recovery mechanism is stated two incompatible ways: AC2 has the review-bot ABSTAIN (cast NO LLM-Review content vote) on infra-unhealthy, but the epic design and AC3 describe recovery as a 'same-patchset re-vote that cleanly REPLACES the stale -1'. If the bot abstains there is no -1 during the blocked window to replace, so the recovery loop's trigger (what it keys on) and target (what it replaces) are under-defined.
findings.location: Epic design bullet 'Recovery = infra-class retry loop … same-patchset re-vote that cleanly REPLACES the stale -1' vs AC2 ('casts no LLM-Review content vote (abstains)') and AC3
scenarios: Infra goes unhealthy, bot abstains vote-less; signal recovers — recovery loop looks for a stale -1 to replace and finds none, so nothing is re-driven
Infra goes unhealthy, bot casts a coverage-gap -1; but AC2 asserts no content vote was emitted — offline test asserting 'no content vote' contradicts the -1
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the existing vote-less-defer shape: on blocking-unhealthy the bot stays vote-less (matching RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS), the Infra-Ready submit-requirement carries the block, and recovery re-drives the vote-less change via the reconciler — dropping the 'replaces the stale -1' language, or reserving it only for the retry-exhaustion terminal -1.

AC3: 'automatically re-run under a bounded retry (RETRY_LIMIT) with windowed replay … asserts exactly one bounded re-run'

The plan does not state whether RETRY_LIMIT is per-signal, per-change, or per-revision, nor whether it replaces, wraps, or nests inside the existing budget.
findings.location: DESIGN → 'Recovery = infra-class retry loop … bounded (RETRY_LIMIT)'; AC3
scenarios: A signal flaps twice for one change: does each flap consume RETRY_LIMIT once, and is that the same counter the reconciler already increments per revision?
AC3 asserts 'exactly one bounded re-run' — undefined counter placement makes this assertion non-deterministic across implementations.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a dependency from S8 (WARN->enforce flip) on S6 (break-glass/waiver) so fail-closed enforcement cannot be enabled before a guaranteed break-glass exists.
evidence: S8 (1de6) deps: depends_on 571e (S5) only
Parent DESIGN: 'a guaranteed break-glass reachable when the gate itself is wedged'
S6 (fad7): 'A guaranteed break-glass reachable even when the gate itself is wedged... Bounds the "all work stops" blast radius'
Parent principle: infra-class block is fail-closed
findings.finding: S8 (1de6) flips the gate from WARN to fail-closed (enforce) but depends only on S5 (571e); it has no dependency on S6 (fad7, break-glass/waiver) or S2 (a0d0, durable config-applied status). Enabling enforce without the guaranteed break-glass (S6) landed first creates an owned-by-none ordering gap: the parent explicitly requires a break-glass 'reachable when the gate itself is wedged' to bound the 'all work stops' blast radius, yet nothing sequences S6 before the S8 enforce flip.
scenarios: S8 flips to fail-closed enforcement in the field before S6's break-glass ships; a wedged gate then halts all landings with no escape hatch - the exact blast radius S6 exists to bound
findings.suggested_fix: Add depends_on 1de6->fad7 (and consider ->a0d0 for the config-applied durable status) so the enforce flip is sequenced after break-glass and the durable config signal land.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either narrow parent AC4 to the config-applied signal, or extend S7 so every wired signal (llm-provider, github, config-valid, deploy-host, environment) binds its observation to a revision/generation and rejects stale readings.
evidence: Parent AC4: 'Each health observation is bound to the config revision it was computed against and a stale observation is rejected rather than allowed to false-clear'
S2 (a0d0) description: 'bound to the config revision it was computed against (Terraform stale-plan rejection)' - scoped to the config-applied probe only
S7 (1028) description: 'Each an independent tri-state probe with blocking/advisory severity' - no mention of revision-binding or stale-rejection
findings.finding: Parent AC4 requires EACH health observation to be bound to its config revision with stale observations rejected, but only S2 (config-applied signal) delivers revision-binding/stale-rejection; the other signals wired by S7 (llm-provider, github, config-valid, deploy-host/replication, environment) are described only as 'independent tri-state probe with blocking/advisory severity' and do not assert revision-binding or stale-rejection. This is scope-narrowing / partial-without-remainder: AC4 says 'Each' but the guarantee lands for one signal only.
scenarios: An llm-provider or github probe returns a stale/cached healthy reading after conditions changed; nothing in S7 rejects the stale observation, so it could false-clear the gate - exactly the failure AC4 forbids, but only for non-config signals
findings.suggested_fix: Add to S7's scope a generation/revision stamp per observation and a stale-rejection rule mirroring S2, or reword AC4 to scope revision-binding to config-derived signals only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that S3's submit-requirement is emitted in WARN/detect-only (non-blocking) until the S8 config flip enables fail-closed, and make the enforce flip explicitly govern S3's blocking behavior.
